ItemResult.description:
A catalog item from the property's shared catalog (MFD).

Inventory fields (``quantity``, ``reorder_threshold``, ``reorder_needed``,
``stop_sell_threshold``, ``stop_sell_reached``) are populated only for
stock-tracked items (``tracks_inventory`` true); they are ``None`` /
``False`` otherwise. ``stop_sell_threshold`` is the "stop selling when
remaining quantity reaches N" cut-off, and ``stop_sell_reached`` whether the
item is at/under it.

**Pricing.** ``price`` is tax-INCLUSIVE, so it is neither net nor gross:
``grand_total`` is ``price`` plus the *exclusive* taxes/fees, and
``price_excluding_taxes_and_fees`` is ``price`` minus the *inclusive* ones.
Show ``grand_total`` as what the guest pays — never ``price + total_taxes``,
which double-counts inclusive tax. ``taxes`` / ``fees`` are the per-charge
breakdown for display; a tax nested under a fee arrives with an extended
name like ``"Sales Tax -> Resort Fee"``.

Every pricing field is always present: an item with no applicable tax or fee
reports empty lists, zero totals, and both derived prices equal to ``price``.
All amounts are for **quantity 1** in the property's currency — MFD rounds
with the quantity inside its allocation, so an N-line total computed as
``amount * N`` is an estimate, not MFD's authoritative figure.
ItemResult.title: ItemResult

OrderItemRequest.description:
One requested line item.

``item_id`` is an **MFD catalog id** (a numeric string such as
``"255051443901120"``), the same id space `GET /pos/items` and
`GET /pos/outlets/{id}/items` return. It is validated against the MFD catalog
at write time; it is not a local ``items.id`` UUID.

``unit_price`` and ``name`` are taken from the client as-is — the POS UI is
the source of truth for what was actually charged, so a later catalog price
change never rewrites history on an existing order.

``unit_price`` is the base price before modifiers. The response's ``unit_price``
includes modifier upcharges, so edits should send its ``base_unit_price``.

``unit_price`` is the **list price** — what the item sells for before any
offer. NEVER the post-offer price. A percentage offer is computed server-side
from this base, so a client that pre-discounts the price it sends gets the
offer taken off twice: once by itself and once by the engine (30% off a
21.00 that was already 30% off a 30.00). The offer's effect on the line is
the server's answer, persisted in ``reductions`` and returned as
``line_total``; the client states what it *showed* via
``claimed_offer_amount`` and the server refuses a mismatch rather than
silently repricing.

The price is client-authoritative; the **offer discount** is not. Offers are
evaluated server-side from the property's own configuration (``offer_service``)
and checked per line (``claimed_offer_amount``) and per cart
(``CreateOrderRequest.claimed_offer_total``), so a client cannot invent a
saving — while a later catalog price change still never rewrites history. Two
different quantities: what the guest was shown, and what the property agreed
to take off.

order_item_id.description: Update only: the existing line this entry replaces (the response's `id`). Matched lines keep this ID across edits; new lines receive new IDs. Ignored on create.

OrderResponse.description:
Full order representation.

**Reading the money.** ``total`` is what the guest pays.
``exclusive_tax_fee_total`` is the part that was ADDED to the item prices;
``inclusive_tax_fee_total`` was already inside them. Those two are the
authoritative split — a per-charge ``treatment`` label can disagree with them
in compound cases (an inclusive tax on a fee, or a tax-on-tax double emission),
because the calculator echoes that flag from configuration rather than deriving
it from what it did. Render from the labels; reconcile from these totals.

``totals_basis`` records how the numbers were produced: ``engine`` (the tax
service), ``no_tax_configured``, ``estimated_offline`` (a replayed offline
order, pending reconciliation), or ``unknown`` for orders predating tax.
OrderResponse.title: OrderResponse

**``connection_type`` is deliberately absent.** POS-103 requires a change of
transport to go back through the pairing wizard rather than being a silent

reachability, different discovery and a different test-print result, and
nothing here could verify the new transport works. Re-pairing is
delete-and-add, which forces the wizard's test print.

``address`` and ``port`` ARE editable — a DHCP lease moving a printer to a
new IP is the single most common real-world repair, and forcing a re-pair
for it would mean re-entering a name and location that did not change.

PropertySettingsResponse.description:
The property's money and scheduling context.

``currency_code`` is ISO 4217 and always present — a property whose currency
cannot be resolved is a 503, never a guess, because the wrong currency
mis-scales every amount rather than merely mislabelling it (JPY has no minor
units, KWD has three). See ``property_service``.

``timezone`` is an IANA name and MAY be null: MFD does not always supply one,
and callers degrade to UTC rather than fail. It is what an offer's happy-hour
window is evaluated against, so a client that has it evaluates "is this offer
live" in the property's own wall clock instead of the device's.

**Display formats are deliberately absent.** Symbol placement, decimal
separators and date order are locale-derived; MFD exposes no per-property
field for them, so inventing one here would create a second source of truth
against whatever it eventually offers. ``currency_code`` is enough to drive
``Intl.NumberFormat`` on the client.

QuoteOfferBlockedResponse.description:
One offer that did NOT apply to this cart, and why.

Exists so the client can explain a not-yet-qualifying offer instead of
letting a cashier choose one the order will refuse with a 422 — the
minimum-spend gate was invisible to the UI, and the dead end surfaced at the
till with the guest standing there. ``minimum_spend`` is carried so a
"spend X to unlock" hint needs no second request and no client-side rules.

``reason`` values are the stable strings ``offer_service.is_active_at`` and
``evaluate`` produce: ``minimum_spend_not_met``, ``outlet_not_included``,
``outside_schedule``, ``outside_date_range``, ``inactive``. One entry per
offer, and never for an offer the cart is eligible for — a per-line coverage
miss (``item_not_covered``) is not a cart-level lock and is reported by the
line itself pricing at gross.
QuoteOfferBlockedResponse.title: QuoteOfferBlockedResponse

QuoteResponse.description:
What a cart would cost if it were ordered now.

Same money semantics as ``OrderResponse``: ``exclusive_tax_fee_total`` was
added on top of the item prices, ``inclusive_tax_fee_total`` was already inside
them, and those totals — not a per-charge ``treatment`` label — are the
authority on the split.

``offers_applied`` is already inside ``discount_total``; it is the breakdown, not
an extra charge. ``offers_available`` names offers that are live and eligible but
do NOT auto-apply — a cashier chooses those — so a client can present them
without evaluating any offer rules itself. ``offers_blocked`` names the ones
that did not qualify and why, so the same client can explain a locked offer
("spend 50.00 to unlock") — again without evaluating any rule itself.

``order_discount_requires_approval`` (and ``requires_approval`` per line) report
a discount above the property's ceiling. The figures still include it — the
quote prices what the cashier rang — but the order will accept it only through
its guarded endpoint with a manager's approval token. Reported rather than
refused because a preview cannot be approved: the token is scoped to an order
or line id that exists only once the order is created, so a 422 here left the
client with a cart it could neither price nor take payment for.
QuoteResponse.title: QuoteResponse

TableResponse.description:
A table within an outlet, including its floor-plan geometry.

``x`` / ``y`` / ``width`` / ``height`` are unpacked from the stored
``grid_position`` JSON and ``kind`` comes from the table's ``format``, using
the same names as {@link FloorPlanTableResponse} so a client can read
geometry from either route. A table that was never positioned (no
``grid_position``) reports zeros rather than null, so consumers can render it
without null checks; ``section_id`` tells the caller which section it sits in.

``section_id`` is the ONLY grouping key — resolve it against
``GET /outlets/{id}/sections`` for a display name. A free-text ``zone`` label
used to ride along here from the pre-sections schema; nothing ever wrote it,
so it was NULL on every row and clients that grouped by it collapsed the whole
floor into one nameless section. Dropped in revision 026.

info.description:
The **Cloudbeds POS API** runs point of sale for a property's restaurants, bars, cafés and other outlets: the menus and catalog an outlet sells, the floor plan it seats, the orders staff take, and how those orders are paid, discounted, split and posted to a guest's folio.

It is the API behind the Cloudbeds POS app and the POS settings in Cloudbeds PMS.

**Key concepts**

- **Outlet** — a place that sells: a restaurant, bar, spa or shop. Outlets own their menus, sections and tables, enabled catalog items, receipt branding and payment options.
- **Catalog** — items and categories come from the property's Cloudbeds catalog. An outlet enables the subset it sells. Orders carry the list price each item sold at; offers, taxes and fees are applied by the server.
- **Order** — a check in progress. It moves `open` → `sent` (fired to the kitchen) → `paid`, or ends `cancelled`. Splitting an order ends it as `split` and creates child orders.
- **Payment** — a tender captured against an order. Several captures can settle one order; once they cover the total, the order becomes `paid`.
- **Folio posting** — a paid order is posted to Cloudbeds as a POS check, with its items, taxes, discounts and gratuity: to the guest's folio for a room charge, to a house account otherwise. Orders settled against a folio chosen in Cloudbeds (`folio`, `group_folio`) are not posted by the POS.
- **Staff, roles and permissions** — staff sign in on a terminal with a PIN. Their role decides what they can do; sensitive actions can be approved by a colleague who holds the permission.

**Authentication**

Every request sends a bearer access token in `Authorization` and the property in `x-property-id`:

- a **Cloudbeds user access token** — management access: outlets, menus, staff, roles and settings;
- a **POS device token** — a paired POS terminal, for taking orders and payments.

Operations that act on behalf of a person also send a **staff token** in `X-Staff-Token`, from `POST /pos/auth/staff/login`. See the Authentication guide.

**Conventions**

- Money is a decimal string or number in the property's currency, with up to three decimal places for currencies that use them. Totals are computed server-side.
- Identifiers are UUIDs unless documented otherwise; catalog item ids are Cloudbeds ids.
- Errors return `{"detail": ...}`: a message, or `{code, message, retryable}` on the charge endpoints. Validation errors (422) list each failing field.
- Writes that must not happen twice take an `Idempotency-Key` header; retrying with the same key returns the original result.
info.title: Cloudbeds POS API
